items.title: Research Paper and Project Implementation
items.summary: Students must find a current research paper topic, implement it, and deploy the resulting project to the cloud.
steps: Write down questions, search for them, and find scenario-based questions.

items.title: Software Defined Approach
items.summary: The lecturer introduces the software-defined approach as a new model for managing resources. Its key function is to abstract the underlying infrastructure, separating the management function from the physical components. This enables centralized control of IT infrastructure like compute, storage, and platform.

items.title: Key Functions of the Software Defined Controller
items.summary: The lecturer begins to list the key functions of the software-defined controller. The first two mentioned are to discover underlying resources and provide an aggregated view of them, and to abstract the underlying hardware resources.

items.title: The Control Layer in Cloud Infrastructure
items.summary: The control layer is a set of software tools responsible for managing and controlling the underlying cloud infrastructure. It receives service requests from the service layer and forwards them down to the virtualization or physical layer to be fulfilled.

items.title: Key Functions of the Control Layer
items.summary: The primary functions of the control layer are to receive requests from the service orchestration layer, provision the required resources, and perform resource configuration, provisioning, and monitoring.

items.title: Role of Control Software
items.summary: Control software ties together underlying resources and works with virtualization. It performs dynamic resource allocation and optimization, provides a complete view of all cloud resources, and centralizes the management of IT resources.

items.title: Types of Control Software: Element Manager vs. Unified Manager
items.summary: There are two types of control software. An element manager manages individual infrastructure components like compute, storage, and fabric independently. A unified manager uses a centralized approach with a single manager to handle all components and balance resources.

items.title: Lower Bond Guarantee and Upper Bond Limit
items.summary: A lower bond guarantees a minimum amount of a resource, while an upper bond limits the maximum amount a service can consume.

items.title: Relative vs. Absolute Resource Allocation
items.summary: The lecturer distinguishes between relative and absolute resource allocation as two different approaches.

items.title: Categories of Resource Management
items.summary: Resource management techniques are categorized into three main areas: compute, storage, and network.

items.title: Hyper-Threading
items.summary: A compute resource management technique where a single physical processor is made to appear as multiple logical cores. This allows an operating system to schedule two threads simultaneously on the same physical core, improving performance and utilization.

items.title: Dynamic Memory Allocation and Page Sharing
items.summary: A memory optimization technique that reclaims memory pages from virtual machines (VMs) that are no longer in use. A hypervisor uses an agent in the guest OS to request and reclaim these pages, returning them to a shared memory pool.
steps: A hypervisor uses an agent installed in the guest OS.
The hypervisor's agent demands memory from the guest OS.
The guest OS allocates memory pages to the agent.
The agent reserves the memory and puts it back into a shared memory pool.

items.title: Dynamic VM Load Balancing Storage Volume
items.summary: A storage technique that intelligently places virtual machines based on input/output load, storage capacity, and performance thresholds to improve server performance and load balancing within a cluster.

items.title: Cluster Volume
items.summary: A collection of one or more volumes that are aggregated into a single volume to enable efficient and rapid placement of new virtual machines.

items.title: Storage Categories
items.summary: The lecture covers different categories of storage, including intra and inter array techniques, cache scaling, dynamic VM load balancing, and cluster volumes.

items.title: Virtual Storage Provisioning
items.summary: The lecturer explains that virtual storage provisioning involves allocating storage to virtual machines (VMs) from a shared storage pool. Each VM is given a virtual allocation (e.g., 10 TB), but they can use more or less than that allocation, drawing from the total capacity of the pool.

items.title: Storage Pool Rebalancing
items.summary: The lecturer describes storage pool rebalancing as a process to distribute data evenly across all physical disk drives in a pool. This is done when new drives are added to help achieve higher overall performance and ensure the capacity of each drive is used uniformly.

items.title: Storage Space Reclamation
items.summary: The lecturer explains that storage space reclamation is the process of reusing space that has been used and then freed up. This is done to provide cost savings by identifying new, unused space and assigning it back to the storage pool. A specific method mentioned is zero extent reclamation, which involves deallocating storage extensions that contain only zeros.

items.title: Automated Storage Steering
items.summary: The lecturer introduces automated storage steering as a technique to automatically store different types of data on the appropriate storage tier. The goal is to ensure that data is placed on the correct storage to meet service level requirements, based on parameters like time frequency.

items.title: Data Movement and Caching in Storage Systems
items.summary: The lecturer explains that data movement in storage systems can occur within a single array (intra-array) or between different arrays (inter-array). This movement is used for cache scaling, where a large capacity secondary cache is created using SSDs, with one tier being SSDs and another being dynamic RAM.

items.title: Unified Manager and Centralized Approach
items.summary: A unified manager uses a centralized approach to manage all things, unlike an element manager which manages everything individually.

items.title: Functionality of a Unified Manager
items.summary: A unified manager provides a single interface for configuration and resource provisioning, exposes APIs for integration with orchestration layers, performs compliance checks, and offers a dashboard for monitoring resource utilization.

items.title: Key Phases of Provisioning
items.summary: The key phases involved in provisioning are resource discovery, resource pool management, and resource provisioning.

items.title: Resource Discovery and Resource Types
items.summary: Resource discovery involves a survey to learn about available resources and providing visibility into the cloud infrastructure. Resources are categorized into compute, network, and storage.
